record.title: VRR uses verification feedback to expand candidate search, with mixed reported benchmark results
record.summary: Tomihari and Ichikawa introduce Verify–Repair–Reselect (VRR), which feeds verifier diagnostics back into generation: after ranking an initial pool, it retains the winner, conditionally creates repairs of the winner and runner-up plus a new-approach candidate, filters invalid/duplicate outputs and reselects under the original criteria. Across two models and eight code/reasoning benchmarks, the authors report VRR beats fixed-pool LAV selection in 9 of 16 settings. Table 1 includes improvements as well as null and negative cells. On LiveCodeBench, the authors report recovery on some problems where all initial candidates were incorrect. These are paper-reported results using the same model for generation, verification and repair; matched total-inference-budget comparison with best-of-N and independent reproduction remain open.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across two models and eight benchmarks, the authors report VRR improves over fixed-pool LAV selection in 9 of 16 settings; Table 1 also contains null and negative settings.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report VRR can recover correct LiveCodeBench solutions when every candidate in the initial pool is incorrect; the recovery result is not independently reproduced.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The same model performs generation, verification, repair and reselection; no matched total-inference-budget comparison against best-of-N was established in this review.

contradictory_evidence: Table 1 reports VRR below fixed-pool LAV for some settings, including -0.61 percentage points on HumanEval+ with Gemma 4 31B IT and -0.27 on MBPP with Qwen3-32B; other cells are tied.

evidence_gaps.description: Reported accuracy results and all-incorrect recovery cases have not been independently reproduced.
Equal-total-inference-compute comparison against best-of-N sampling is missing.

brief.importance_rationale: If reproduced at matched inference budgets, verifier feedback that expands rather than only ranks a candidate set could materially improve test-time search when initial candidates are all incorrect. The paper reports gains in 9 of 16 tested model-benchmark settings and includes null/negative cells; the consequence is notable for inference design, while independent and compute-normalized evidence is absent.
limitations: All results are paper-reported; the research desk did not execute code or independently reproduce the experiments.
VRR improves over fixed-pool LAV in 9 of 16 model-benchmark settings; the table includes null and negative cells.
The same model performs generation, verification, repair and reselection, so verifier errors may be inherited or amplified.
The paper does not establish that gains survive an equal total generation-plus-verification token or latency budget versus best-of-N sampling.
Passing public tests or format filters establishes candidate eligibility, not correctness; reselection can still choose an incorrect answer.
brief.summary: Tomihari and Ichikawa introduce Verify–Repair–Reselect (VRR), which feeds verifier diagnostics back into generation: after ranking an initial pool, it retains the winner, conditionally creates repairs of the winner and runner-up plus a new-approach candidate, filters invalid/duplicate outputs and reselects under the original criteria. Across two models and eight code/reasoning benchmarks, the authors report VRR beats fixed-pool LAV selection in 9 of 16 settings. Table 1 includes improvements as well as null and negative cells. On LiveCodeBench, the authors report recovery on some problems where all initial candidates were incorrect. These are paper-reported results using the same model for generation, verification and repair; matched total-inference-budget comparison with best-of-N and independent reproduction remain open.

technical.claimed_result: The authors argue that verifier diagnostics can improve the candidate set and allow recovery beyond the initial pool. Whether gains persist against best-of-N under equal total generation-plus-verification compute is unresolved.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper evaluates Gemma 4 31B IT and Qwen3-32B across eight code and reasoning benchmarks, using identical frozen initial pools for Single, fixed-pool LAV and VRR. It reports that VRR improves over LAV in 9 of 16 model-benchmark settings. Table 1 includes negative results (for example -0.61 and -0.27 percentage points), null results (0.00) and positive cells (up to +4.04 points in the shown table). LiveCodeBench analysis reports some recovered correct answers even when every initial candidate was incorrect. These are author-reported results.
technical.implementation_status: The paper gives algorithm details, prompt templates and experimental settings. the research desk did not run the code or independently reproduce results.
technical.mechanism: VRR builds explicit evaluation criteria, verifies and ranks a frozen initial candidate set, and triggers repair when scores are low or judgments remain unresolved. It retains the initial winner, generates a local repair, a runner-up repair and a new-approach solution, screens malformed or duplicate candidates, then re-verifies and reselects under the original criteria.
technical.novelty: Uses criterion-level verifier feedback as a signal for expanding the candidate set, while retaining the original winner and applying the same criteria to final reselection.
technical.regime: Two models, eight code/reasoning benchmarks, five initial candidates for code and three for reasoning tasks. The same model performs generation, verification, repair and reselection. Verifier labels and private tests are withheld until answers are fixed; newly generated candidates are checked with public tests and format/duplicate filters.
technical.reproducibility: The paper provides prompt templates and benchmark configuration. Independent reproduction, compute-normalized comparisons, variance, and sensitivity to verifier/generator separation remain open.
technical.strongest_baseline: Fixed-pool LAV selection over the same frozen initial candidates, plus a Single first-candidate baseline. The paper does not establish a matched total-token/latency comparison with best-of-N independent sampling.

brief.title: VRR uses verification feedback to expand candidate search, with mixed reported benchmark results
brief.why_it_matters: Verifier feedback can describe why candidates fail, not just which candidate ranks highest. Reusing that diagnostic information to generate alternatives could improve test-time search when every initial candidate is wrong. The paper’s mixed results, same-model verifier/generator and missing compute-normalized best-of-N comparison mean the gain should be treated as a bounded method result rather than general evidence that repair beats more sampling.
